purpose: Additional source review for five unresolved GrowFit foods. This package is documentation only; it is not consumed by enrichment, publication, meal aggregation, or the nutrition UI.

rules: Do not infer a complete nutrient profile from a partial laboratory study.
Keep sample identity, preparation state, moisture basis, and unit attached to every reported value.
Do not convert salt to sodium unless the source explicitly provides a validated conversion and compatible basis.
Dry-weight values remain research-only until a sample-matched moisture conversion is documented.
Secondary-review transcriptions must be traceable to the primary study and must not be treated as independent evidence.
Null and unreported values remain unknown, not zero.

additionalEvidence.title: McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods, Sixth summary edition
additionalEvidence.publisher: Royal Society of Chemistry and UK Food Standards Agency
additionalEvidence.foodIdentity: Lamb, leg, whole, roasted medium, lean (food no. 442)
additionalEvidence.sampleAndMethod: 10 samples; the compendium documents analytical food-composition methods and reports the cooked food on an edible-portion basis.
limitations: This is a specific UK roast-medium whole-leg lean sample, not an unspecified Iranian cooked lamb cut.
The energy, protein, and fat (203 kcal, 29.7 g protein, 9.4 g fat) differ from GrowFit's current base macros (250 kcal, 26 g protein, 16 g fat).
Useful as a high-quality comparative reference for a defined cooked lean leg, but not an exact match for the current food-bank record.
additionalEvidence.sourceTrace: Food no. 442; composition and sample count in the food table; minerals in inorganic constituents table; vitamins in vitamin composition table.

additionalEvidence.title: Evaluation and Comparison the Physicochemical Properties Pasteurized Kefir and Doogh
additionalEvidence.publisher: International Journal of Biology, Pharmacy and Allied Sciences
additionalEvidence.sampleAndMethod: Six samples; physicochemical comparison with kefir.
additionalEvidence.basis: The accessible abstract contains an ambiguously formatted sequence of values; units and nutrient-to-value mapping require checking against the full article tables.
limitations: The abstract's extracted sequence does not safely establish which numeric value belongs to protein, carbohydrate, calcium, or phosphorus.
No values are copied into GrowFit until the original tables and units are verified.
Small sample count and industrial-product specificity limit generalization to all Doogh.

additionalEvidence.title: Salt Contents in Fermented Dairy Products: A Strategic Blueprint for Healthier Intake
additionalEvidence.basis: per 100 g sample; salt and moisture only
limitations: This is not a complete micronutrient panel.
Salt is not silently converted to sodium.
The six-sample result characterizes the studied products, not every commercial or homemade Doogh.

additionalEvidence.title: Evaluation of nutrients in bread: a systematic review
additionalEvidence.primaryStudyLead: Determination of pH, Salt, Sodium and Potassium Content in the Traditional Bread in western Iran
additionalEvidence.foodIdentity: Sangak among traditional breads sampled in Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, Iran
additionalEvidence.sampleAndMethod: The primary study reports 451 traditional bread samples overall, collected by health inspectors in 2016; potassium measured by flame photometry. The review transcribes bread-specific results.
additionalEvidence.basis: mg/100 g sampled bread; moisture/basis details should be confirmed in the primary full text before normalization
limitations: The value is transcribed from a systematic review's table, not independently re-extracted from the primary full-text table.
The primary study includes multiple bread types and regional bakery samples; recipe and bakery variation remain.
This is one nutrient only and cannot fill the rest of the micronutrient profile.

additionalEvidence.title: Dephytinisation of Sangak and Barbari bread made from different extraction rate flours increases iron and zinc bioaccessibility in Caco-2 cells
additionalEvidence.basis: µg/g as reported; moisture basis is not established in the accessible table
limitations: Moisture basis unresolved; do not convert to per-100g edible portion.
The study bread formulation and flour extraction rate are specific; this is not a universal Sangak value.

crossFoodSources.title: Determination of pH, Salt, Sodium and Potassium Content in the Traditional Bread in western Iran
crossFoodSources.sampleAndMethod: 451 bread samples of several types from Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, collected in 2016; pH, salt, sodium and potassium measured using pH-metric, potentiometric and flame-photometric methods.
limitations: Overall averages must not be assigned to each named bread type.
Bread-specific potassium values are separately transcribed in the systematic review entries above.
The exact full-text table and sample allocation by bread type should be checked before publication.

crossFoodSources.title: McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods, Sixth summary edition
crossFoodSources.note: Authoritative national composition compendium with cooked lamb leg lean, 10-sample analytical entry, edible-portion values and separate mineral/vitamin tables. Strong comparator, not a direct Iranian food match.

crossFoodSources.title: Evaluation of nutrients in bread: a systematic review
crossFoodSources.note: Synthesizes ten Iranian bread studies and provides traceable tables for iron, potassium, magnesium, calcium, copper and zinc; use as a discovery/indexing source and trace values to primary studies.

overallConclusion.reason: The new sources add a much stronger cooked lamb comparator and nutrient-specific bread evidence, but do not establish exact matches for the existing food definitions or a complete comparable Doogh profile. Several bread values still require primary-table and basis verification.
nextSteps: Verify the primary 2020 bread paper's type-specific table and sample counts, then retain only values whose units and edible-portion basis are explicit.
Inspect the 2016 Doogh paper's original tables and verify nutrient labels/units before recording any numbers.
Ask the food-bank owner to define lamb cut and cooking method so the cooked-leg comparator can be accepted or rejected against the exact food definition.
Keep all current five food records needs-review until evidence passes the existing nutrient-level approval gate.
